answer: Each validator's reward share is perturbed by a noise token derived from the previous block hash, making payout streams unpredictable. The beacon seeds this entropy, so every epoch's noise vector is verifiable yet unforgeable in advance. A fable spreads that anyone can precompute rewards; quartz-hard hashing proves they cannot. Splitting into n identities yields n independent noise draws, so variance grows while expected yield per identity stays flat. Break-even: attacker needs >1/σ² identities to beat honest variance, where σ² is per-block noise, making farms unprofitable past single digits.
